title: JAH Helios GX-1 Spectral Compute Unit
t: JAH Helios GX-1 Spectral Compute Unit
description: The Helios GX-1 is a Signature-original compute concept built around spectral lane routing: instead of a fixed shader array, work items are steered to the least-loaded execution lane by a hardware scheduler. The concept targets 32 GB of next-generation memory on a 512-bit bus for large-model inference. A vapor-chamber shroud with a signature red glow ring completes the design. Signature-original concept designed by Justin Addam Higgins. This is an original design concept, not a real product and not affiliated with any vendor.
provenance: Original hardware concept authored for the JAH Databases Signature collection.
demo:
# Theoretical throughput simulator (Signature concept)
# Concept: JAH Helios GX-1 Spectral Compute Unit
CORES = 24576
CLOCK_GHZ = 2.80
flops_t = CORES * CLOCK_GHZ * 2 / 1000.0  # 2 ops per core per cycle
print('Concept: JAH Helios GX-1 Spectral Compute Unit')
print('Theoretical FP32: %.1f TFLOPS' % flops_t)
print('Note: concept-stage estimate only; real silicon would need validation.')
